summary: The TPS25751 test board as source and an iPhone as sink, after a port_reset. Both the capture and registers.json are real: the tps25751-pd-verify skill recorded the capture and took the bench console's SNAP after the contract.

setup.source: TPS25751 test board on its battery, configured from its EEPROM, held in the Source role for the session (see session_writes)
setup.sink: iPhone (Apple, USB Vendor ID 0x05AC, Product ID 0x710C, bcdDevice 0x2166 in its Discover Identity ACK)
setup.cabling: Board into the KM003C's receptacle (input), the meter's plug into the iPhone; the meter's host USB cable connected throughout
setup.cable: The passive cable of Phase 6. Its SOP' Discover Identity ACK reports VDOs 1c0020c2 00000000 00070310 31082052: USB Vendor ID 0x20C2, Product ID 0x0007, bcdDevice 0x0310, Passive Cable, with a PD 2.0 header and SVDM version 1.0
setup.stimulus: bench_renegotiate port_reset (rewrite of 0x28 with its current value), skill argument stop identity
setup.firmware: examples/pd-bench of library 3.2.0 with the bench console of branch feat/pd-verify-skill; controller VERSION 0xF8091166
setup.operator: Library maintainer at the bench; the tps25751-pd-verify skill ran headless in Claude Code

session_writes.name: PORT_CONFIGURATION
session_writes.why: TypeC State Machine (bits 1:0) Source only instead of DRP, so the board attaches as Source to the iPhone

session_writes.name: PORT_CONTROL
session_writes.why: Bits 5 (Initiate Swap to Sink) and 4 (Process Swap to Sink) cleared, so the board neither sends nor accepts a PR_Swap to Sink

capture.command: km003c MCP server pd_capture_start with stop_on none, timeout_s 120; stopped by the skill with pd_capture_stop
notes: The header's provenance names stimulus port_reset, stop identity, role source, lib 3.2.0, version f8091166.

The board sent Source_Capabilities with PDO 1 0x0301912C, where 0x32 holds 0x2001912C: bits 29 (Dual-Role Power), 25 (Dual-Role Data), and 24 (Unchunked Extended Messages) differ, set by the controller at runtime. PDOs 2 to 5 equal 0x32.
The iPhone made two contracts on PDO 1: Request RDO 0x1784B12C, then 0x1384B12C. Its Discover Identity ACK (VID 0x05AC) came between them, and the board's own ACK (VID 0x0451) after the second.

registers.how: bench_snapshot(path=...) of the tps25751-bench MCP server: the console's SNAP command, length bytes as read
notes: STATUS (0x1A) 6f00200000: plug present, port role Source.
0x34 reads 0x0301912C in bits 31:0, the PDO 1 the board sent, and 0x200 in bits 41:32, which equals 0x32 PDO 1 bits 29:20 rather than the 0x030 of the PDO 1 on the wire.
0x35 reads the iPhone's final Request, 0x1384B12C, in both bits 31:0 and bits 127:96.
0x30 reads one PDO of 0x00000000: the board received no Source_Capabilities in this attach.
